notes:
I couldn't write the Amos 1 notes because the research tools stopped working before I could read any sources.

My first attempt to fetch the pages (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, and the Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Amos at New Advent) returned an error saying I had no more tool calls left. A second try failed the same way, so no page content ever came back. My other tools have no internet access.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point, so I haven't written anything. Notes written from my own knowledge would break that rule, and I'd have no real URLs to give.

If you send the request again in a new turn, I'll read these pages and write the verse-by-verse notes:
- **Traditional reading:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/amos-1/, Bible Hub's Ellicott, Pulpit and Gill commentaries on Amos 1, and Precept Austin's Amos 1 commentary.
- **Protestant traditions:** Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon and Desiring God, Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition, and Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org).
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes on "three transgressions, even four," Kir, Aven and Beth-eden; Bible Odyssey; and New Advent and catholic.com for Catholic readings.

Another option is to paste in the text of any of these pages, and I'll write the notes from that.
